title: How CBT sessions work in practice
citation: Hofmann, S. G., Asnaani, A., Vonk, I. J., Sawyer, A. T., & Fang, A. (2012). The efficacy of cognitive behavioral therapy: A review of meta-analyses. Cognitive therapy and research, 36(5), 427-440.
content:
How CBT sessions work in practice.

CBT sessions are usually collaborative, with the therapist and client working together to understand current difficulties and agree on practical goals. Sessions often include reviewing recent experiences, learning new strategies, practising skills during the session, and planning small exercises to try between appointments. Progress is reviewed regularly so that therapy can be adapted to what is most helpful. Over time, many people develop skills they can continue using long after therapy has ended.
